risks.title: Payments may cluster just below procurement route boundaries
risks.statement: Payment values observed close to the printed quote and tender boundaries warrant checking that the correct procurement route was followed.

likelihood.justification: Payments flagged near printed value boundaries recur across many payees and every month observed: {{$.tests.threshold_clustering.count}} distinct payments [metric:$.tests.threshold_clustering.count], against the quote requirement [rule:CPR-68]. Most sit at the lowest boundary, where recurring care and grant payments can legitimately repeat. The statutory thresholds are not supplied, so those boundaries are untested. This supports the recurring-indicator level and no higher [history:LIKELIHOOD-3].

impact.justification: A wrong route at the lower value bands would mostly involve modest sums, which fits the minor financial descriptor [history:IMPACT-2]. The route requirement is set by [rule:CPR-68]. Data on actual consequences is not available, and spend is not treated as loss.

risks.proposed_focus: Compare flagged payments with the quotation and invitation records for the matching band, and separate recurring placement and grant payments from one-off purchases.

risks.title: Related requirements may not be aggregated for procurement purposes
risks.statement: Repeated payments to the same payee within short windows warrant checking whether related requirements were aggregated, as the anti-avoidance rule requires.

likelihood.justification: The test found {{$.tests.split_purchases.count}} general-procurement windows [metric:$.tests.split_purchases.count] across several payees and months, which is a recurring indicator [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. The population covers only payments over the publication floor, so this is a lower bound. Periodic care and education fees can legitimately recur, and these are reported separately. Statutory-threshold windows were not tested because the parameters are null. The governing requirement is [rule:CPR-12].

impact.justification: Disaggregation could mean contracts above a competition boundary were not competed, which fits external agency criticism and a reasonable possibility of legal challenge [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-12]. No consequence data exists, and the windows are indicators, not proven avoidance.

risks.proposed_focus: Sample windows for general-procurement payees and trace each to the underlying requirement, order and approval to see whether one need was bought in parts.

risks.title: Supplier spend may lack a matching published contract notice
risks.statement: Many paid suppliers have no matching published notice, so contract and advertising coverage needs checking against the council's own contract register.

likelihood.justification: Of the {{$.tests.off_contract.eligible_suppliers}} suppliers large enough to be classed [metric:$.tests.off_contract.eligible_suppliers], {{$.matching.none}} supplier names across the spend population had no matching active notice [metric:$.matching.none], so the indicator is widespread. The notice file is a Contracts Finder export and not a contract register. Awards made earlier, awards advertised elsewhere and exempt placements will also show no notice, so this is an indicator to check and not evidence of off-contract spend. The relevant requirements are [rule:CPR-70] and [rule:CPR-07]. The rubric level is recurring indicators across suppliers [history:LIKELIHOOD-3].

impact.justification: Missing notices or an incomplete register could expose the council to criticism on transparency and a reasonable possibility of regulatory interest [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-70]. The consequence is unknown until the register is compared, and spend totals are not treated as loss.

risks.proposed_focus: Obtain the council's contract register and match the unmatched high-value payees to it. Confirm that the contract-notice and register-publication duties have been met.

risks.title: Payments may have been made more than once for the same amount and payee
risks.statement: Groups of same-payee, same-amount payments within a short window warrant checking against invoices for possible duplicate payment.

likelihood.justification: {{$.tests.duplicates.count}} groups were found [metric:$.tests.duplicates.count] across many payees and all months observed, which is a recurring indicator [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. Many groups are care and education placement payments, where several service users can share the same fee. Whether any are duplicates needs invoice-level evidence, which this data does not hold. The relevant control is written evidence of purchases [rule:CPR-32]. A recent accounts payable audit reported reasonable assurance and is not adverse [history:AUD-15].

impact.justification: Confirmed duplicates would mean overpayment and possible external criticism of payment controls [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-32]. The beyond-first-instance value is an indicator, not a loss, and no recovery or consequence data is available.

risks.proposed_focus: Select groups across both timestamp tiers and agree each payment to its invoice, order and goods or service receipt. Establish whether duplicate checks run before payment release.

risks.title: Payments may continue after the published award has ended
risks.statement: Payments to payees whose published awards all ended before the period warrant checking for an approved extension or a newer contract.

likelihood.justification: The indicator is limited: {{$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count}} payees matched exactly to notices that had all ended [metric:$.tests.expired_notice_spend.count]. That is an isolated indicator [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. A newer contract may exist without a published notice, so the figure may overstate the position. Extensions need the approval in [rule:CPR-78].

impact.justification: The values involved are small relative to the council's budget bands, which fits the minor financial descriptor [history:IMPACT-2]. Unapproved extensions would breach [rule:CPR-78]. No consequence data is available.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged payee, obtain the current contract or extension approval and confirm it was authorised by the required officer.

risks.title: Spend may exceed the annual rate of the published award value
risks.statement: Payees whose annualised spend is well above the published award's annual rate warrant checking for undocumented variation or scope growth.

likelihood.justification: Only {{$.tests.spend_vs_award.count}} payees met the eligibility rules and exceeded the ratio [metric:$.tests.spend_vs_award.count], an isolated indicator [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. Most payees could not be tested because they lacked a single active notice, and award values may be estimates or maxima. Variations need approval under [rule:CPR-79] and [rule:CPR-80].

impact.justification: Unapproved variations could be challenged as breaching the approval and competition rules, which fits the reasonable-possibility-of-challenge descriptor [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-80]. The statutory threshold that sets the approver is not supplied. No consequence data exists, and the excess is not treated as loss.

risks.proposed_focus: For each flagged contract, compare payments to the award and any variation or extension records, and confirm the approver required by the variation rules signed off.

risks.title: Waivers, exceptions and approvals may not be fully documented
risks.statement: Waiver and exception approvals and their documentation cannot be seen in spend data, and the rules give conflicting waiver authority, so they need testing by enquiry and document review.

likelihood.justification: No metric observes waivers, exception reports or approvals, so this rests on the rules and the gap. The rules require documented waivers [rule:CPR-25] and approval by a named officer [rule:CPR-27]. They are inconsistent on who may waive, since [rule:CPR-20] allows executive discretion while [rule:CPR-21] limits waivers to two officers. This is above the rule-only level because the wording conflict is itself an indicator, and no adverse audit evidence was found [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. A recent contract letting audit gave reasonable assurance [history:AUD-01].

impact.justification: Undocumented or wrongly authorised waivers could draw external agency criticism and a reasonable possibility of legal challenge [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-21]. The scale of waiver use is unknown because no waiver register data was supplied.

risks.proposed_focus: Request the waiver and exception register and a sample of exception reports. Test authority, advance timing and recorded reasons, and clarify which officer's approval applies.

risks.theme: Care and education placement choice records
risks.title: Provider choice for exempt placements may not be recorded
risks.statement: Placement spend is exempt from competition on condition that the reasons for the choice of provider are recorded, and the data cannot show whether this was done.

likelihood.justification: This is a rule-only control with no observable metric: the record of provider choice is required by [rule:CPR-81] and sits in case notes outside the spend data. No adverse evidence was found, so the rating is an isolated-indicator level [history:LIKELIHOOD-2]. A recent audit of residential and nursing care purchasing gave reasonable assurance [history:AUD-18].

impact.justification: Placement spend is the largest tagged group in the population, and weak provider-choice records could attract external agency criticism of value for money [history:IMPACT-3] [rule:CPR-81]. Consequence data is not available.

risks.proposed_focus: Sample placement payments and check that case notes record the reasons for provider choice, including recurring payments and any provider paid across several services.

risks.title: A limited-assurance audit of personal budget payments may bear on payment controls
risks.statement: A recent audit of direct payments gave an adverse opinion and no agreed actions are published, so the status of improvements is unknown.

likelihood.justification: An adverse overall opinion is current evidence of weak controls over a payment stream [history:AUD-16]. No paper lists agreed actions, owners or due dates, so progress cannot be confirmed. This differs from the supplier-payment population tested here and is not claimed as a repeat finding on any theme above. It is rated at the recurring level because adverse assurance exists and follow-up is unseen [history:LIKELIHOOD-3]. The related payment control is [rule:CPR-32].

impact.justification: Adverse assurance on payments to individuals fits external agency criticism of control weakness [history:IMPACT-3] [history:AUD-16]. The consequence is not quantified in the papers, and the population may fall outside the published spend extract.

risks.proposed_focus: Ask for the agreed actions and implementation status from that audit and check whether any of the weaknesses apply to supplier payments in scope.
